newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria FEI Bank has 525 mln lev 96 gross profit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria FEI Bank has 525 mln lev 96 gross profit.

text.p: Bulgaria's private First East International Bank (FEIB) posted 525 million levs gross profit for 1996 after a 13.8 million lev gross profit for 1995, a senior bank official said on Thursday.

"The total gross profit of 525 million levs for last year will be set aside for provisions against the bank's non-performing loans," FEIB executive board chairman Anna Sabeva told a meeting of FEIB shareholders.
The profit resulted from translation gains of foreign currency assets and liabilities into levs, Sabeva added. @
The bank's provisions against bad debts totalled 1.1 billion levs at the end of last year, lower than the required 3.8 billion levs, figures from the auditors' report showed.
The lev fell to about 500 to the dollar at the end of last year from around 70 at the beginning of January 1996.
Credits extended by FEIB to financial institutions, individuals and companies totalled 14.2 billion levs at the end of 1996.
The bank's total assets amounted to 31 billion levs at the end of 1996, of which financial assets were 23.8 billion levs. @
FEIB capital-to-risk assets ratio rose to 8.8 percent at end-April from 1.7 percent at the end of 1996 after the bank covered central bank provisioning requirements, Sabeva said.
Under a $657 million funding agreement signed with the International Monetary Fund Bulgarian banks should have a minimum six percent capital-to-risk ratio by the end of this year.
Funds attracted by FEIB totalled 26 billion levs at the end of 1996. @
The bank's own capital totalled 4.57 billion levs at the end of last year. The share capital amounted to 3.0 billion levs, of which 2.2 billion levs were paid in.

The shareholders authorised the supervisory board to raise capital to 25 billion levs by the year 2001 through new share issues in line with an anticipated rise of central bank minimum capital requirements.
The minimum capital required for domestic banking operations is now set at 1.4 billion levs and at 2.2 billion levs for local and international operations. @
Sabeva said negotiations were under way for the sale of 15 percent of FEIB to a Russian state-owned bank and another five percent to a Russian company.
She declined to elaborate, saying the Bulgarian National Bank has yet to decide whether to allow those two potential investors to acquire stakes in FEIB. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
